This section reports the hash-bound gate records and the released curves, bound to the receipt of their effective release, together with the complete inventory. 
The run is an evaluation, on new seeds, of a protocol amended after partial calibration exposure, not a fully blind confirmation. 
The whole curve over the nine values of $r$ is the primary result, and no value of $r$ is selected or used to summarize it. 
At the effective release on \resultnum{v4.release.effective_local}{[time]} America/Sao\_Paulo, triggered by \resultnum{v4.release.condition}{[condition]} against the nominal close of \resultnum{v4.protocol.close_local}{18 October 2026 at 23:59} America/Sao\_Paulo, \resultnum{v4.inv.n_valid}{[n]} of the \resultnum{v4.protocol.units.all}{414} units of the frozen inventory were complete valid (\texttt{completo válido}), \resultnum{v4.inv.n_invalid}{[n]} complete invalid (\texttt{completo inválido}), \resultnum{v4.inv.n_partial}{[n]} partial at operational close (\texttt{parcial por encerramento operacional}) and \resultnum{v4.inv.n_not_started}{[n]} not started (\texttt{não iniciado}) (Table~\ref{tab:v4-T4}, Fig.~\ref{fig:v4-F5}). 
The tiers ran in their fixed order, which no AUC, band width or invalidity changed, and the declared-close rule requires any unfinished work to stop. 
Only complete units contribute boundaries and AUC profiles; every other unit appears in the inventory with its status. 
All nine tier-\resultnum{v4.protocol.tier.main_B}{1} units of B were complete valid, so the main curve is valid under the frozen rule. 
Against B, the first boundary was small ($\resultnum{v4.protocol.a.0}{0}<a^*\le \resultnum{v4.protocol.small_cut}{0.03}$) at \resultnum{v4.t1.n_small}{[n]} values of $r$, large ($\resultnum{v4.protocol.small_cut}{0.03}<a^*\le \resultnum{v4.protocol.a.090}{0.90}$) at \resultnum{v4.t1.n_large}{[n]}, not attained on a complete eligible grid at \resultnum{v4.t1.n_not_attained}{[n]}, and censored or indeterminate at \resultnum{v4.t1.n_censored}{[n]} (Fig.~\ref{fig:v4-F1}, Fig.~\ref{fig:v4-F2B}, Table~\ref{tab:v4-T1}). 
The cut at \resultnum{v4.protocol.small_cut}{0.03} is an internal convention, not a demonstrated effect size, and boundaries are grid strengths, not continuous estimates. 
The attained first boundaries ranged from $a=\resultnum{v4.t1.first_min}{[a]}$ to $a=\resultnum{v4.t1.first_max}{[a]}$, and at every value of $r$ where $a^*$ was attained the sustained boundary equalled it. 
The lower band exceeded \resultnum{v4.protocol.target}{0.70} at some strength at \resultnum{v4.t1.n_crossing}{[n]} values of $r$; ``crossing'' refers only to such strengths. 
The inverted interval of $a^*$ spanned at most one grid step at all \resultnum{v4.t1.n_attained}{[n]} values of $r$ at which $a^*$ was attained, which meets the frozen precision target; that target is a planning goal, not a statement of power. 
The global requirements for a cross-mechanism sentence were not met: tier \resultnum{v4.protocol.tier.main_others}{2} must be entirely complete valid and the main curve valid. No local or headline reading compares mechanisms; all valid units retain their tables and figures. 
Fig.~\ref{fig:v4-F1} and Table~\ref{tab:v4-T1} show B and the state-dependent persistence null D side by side at all \resultnum{v4.bd.n_side_by_side}{[n]} signal shares ($r=$ \resultnum{v4.bd.r_side_by_side}{[r list]}). The frozen reading and every paired count below use the common set of \resultnum{v4.bd.n_eligible}{[n]} values with both units gap-free ($r=$ \resultnum{v4.bd.r_eligible}{[r list]}). 
Within that common set, first boundaries were small, large, not attained or censored/indeterminate at \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_small}{[n]}, \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_large}{[n]}, \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_not_attained}{[n]} and \resultnum{v4.bd.B.n_censored}{[n]} values against B, and at \resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_small}{[n]}, \resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_large}{[n]}, \resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_not_attained}{[n]} and \resultnum{v4.bd.D.n_censored}{[n]} against D. 
At \resultnum{v4.bd.n_inconclusive}{[n]} of these values of $r$ ($r=$ \resultnum{v4.bd.r_inconclusive}{[r list]}) the lower band against B exceeded \resultnum{v4.protocol.target}{0.70} at some strength while the band against D reached \resultnum{v4.protocol.target}{0.70} without its lower limit exceeding it; under the frozen rule, the comparison at these values is inconclusive. 
At \resultnum{v4.bd.n_both}{[n]} of these values of $r$ ($r=$ \resultnum{v4.bd.r_both}{[r list]}) the lower bands against both B and D exceeded \resultnum{v4.protocol.target}{0.70} at some strength; the protocol registers no contrast between null families, so no reading about partner drift is attached to the relative position of the two boundaries. 
At \resultnum{v4.bd.n_no_b_crossing}{[n]} of these values of $r$ ($r=$ \resultnum{v4.bd.r_no_b_crossing}{[r list]}) the lower band against B did not exceed \resultnum{v4.protocol.target}{0.70} at any strength, so the frozen reading does not apply there. 
These readings concern the fixed lag-three to lag-five discriminator and the declared laws; none identifies causal social influence, and the misfit of a null does not identify the generator. 
Against A, C and E the boundaries are shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:v4-F1} and Table~\ref{tab:v4-T1}, with the full profiles in the supplement (Supplementary Figs.~\ref{fig:v4-F2A}, \ref{fig:v4-F2C}, \ref{fig:v4-F2D} and~\ref{fig:v4-F2E}). 
\resultnum{v4.inv.t2.n_invalid}{[n]} tier-\resultnum{v4.protocol.tier.main_others}{2} units are complete invalid, because their zero-strength band excluded \resultnum{v4.protocol.null_auc}{0.5} or their zero-strength cell was a gap; their boundaries are suppressed, and no null family is promoted or demoted. 
Supplementary Fig.~\ref{fig:v4-F3} shows, for the values of $r$ at which both units reached the target, the position of each secondary family's boundary relative to B's in grid steps; it is exploratory and descriptive, with no interval or test. 
Tier \resultnum{v4.protocol.tier.controls}{3} ended with \resultnum{v4.inv.t3.n_valid}{[n]} of its \resultnum{v4.protocol.units.t3}{270} units complete valid and \resultnum{v4.inv.t3.n_incomplete}{[n]} not started or partial (Table~\ref{tab:v4-T4}); units that were not completed are absent and not interpreted. 
No value of $r$ has both an observed unit and any of its masked latent, ordinal at unit signal share or \texttt{latent\_rank} controls complete and valid, so no comparison between channels is reported. 
At none of the \resultnum{v4.t3.n_pairs_compared}{[n]} family-and-$r$ pairs with a valid observed unit and at least one valid control did the observed-channel point AUC exceed any of the three controls at a shared strength (\allunitsresource). 
All units of the sensitivity tiers \resultnum{v4.protocol.tier.first_sensitivity}{4} to \resultnum{v4.protocol.tier.last_sensitivity}{6} were complete valid, and at every value of $r$ their region of $a^*$ matched that of the main B unit (\allunitsresource); the sensitivities are not promoted to a primary analysis. 
The \resultnum{v4.protocol.shp.anchor_year}{2004} reliability of the SHP trust item, estimated by the preregistered quasi-simplex model, was \resultnum{v4.shp.estimate}{[r]} with a Wald \resultnum{v4.protocol.shp.wald_level}{95}\% interval from \resultnum{v4.shp.wald_lo}{[r]} to \resultnum{v4.shp.wald_hi}{[r]}, and the nine Heise triplet estimates ranged from \resultnum{v4.shp.env_lo}{[r]} to \resultnum{v4.shp.env_hi}{[r]}, a specification range rather than a confidence interval (Fig.~\ref{fig:v4-F6}). 
The anchor is drawn on the frozen grid without extrapolating $a^*(r)$; it was not used to choose $r$, strengths, targets or rules, and it is not rounded to a grid value. 
At the \resultnum{v4.shp.n_r_in_interval}{[n]} grid values inside the Wald interval, the B units share one combination of status and region (Table~\ref{tab:v4-T1}). 
The anchor and the simulation's signal share are different quantities (Discussion), and the anchor does not validate the simulated mechanism. 
The empirical max-$t$ critical value did not exceed the \resultnum{v4.protocol.critical_floor}{2.7729} floor in any released curve, and no G2 pipeline raised the covariance-Jacobian flag (\allunitsresource, Table~\ref{tab:v4-T3}). 
Per-cell nuisance diagnostics, namely the mean shift, the Monte Carlo error of the nuisance variance and the fraction of projected draws, are released with every cell. 
Statements about how $a^*$ varies across $r$ are descriptive: the bands are simultaneous within each $r$ only, seeds differ across $r$, and no simultaneous band over all \resultnum{v4.protocol.grid_cells}{81} cells was prespecified.
